answer: Unique Identifier Seeding. Each identity requests a random seed at registration; the network logs every seed ever issued. A clone farm must register many identities, but any two that share a registration context cannot diverge: the system issues seeds from a shared hidden pool, so duplicates surface as collisions across a long horizon. An attacker splitting one real identity into k clones pays k separate seed requests, each exposing a detectable trace in that cedar-colored ledger, and any clone pair that fails to diverge collapses to a single hollow slot.
